LESSON: PHOTOGRAPHY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.4: Photography
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Photography, part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is light important in photography?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Photography together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner selects to store photographs with proper lighting and centre of interest.

Values:
• Respect: Is instilled during group discussions as the learner listens to and accommodates peers’ views.

• Responsibility: Is developed through setting and caring for the digital devices and using digital devices.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Social Cohesion: The learner works with peers’ to take photos of self and objects in the surroundings.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematics: The learner applies mathematical concepts, such as geometry and proportions, in framing and composition.

• Integrated Science: The learner delves into the science behind digital imaging technologies, connecting scientific

principles to the functioning of devices used in photography.
